articles.title: The National Park Service Is Using Flock. Rangers Are Pissed
articles.titleZh: 国家公园管理局在用 Flock 摄像头，护林员很生气
articles.author: Joseph Cox

zh.thesis: 国家公园管理局在公园里安装 Flock 车牌识别摄像头，护林员认为这是对游客隐私的侵犯。
paragraphs: 国家公园管理局在优胜美地等公园装上了 Flock 摄像头。现任和前任护林员都很不满。
「Flock 保护的是财产，不是人和公园。人们应该能自由地以尊重生态的方式游玩，但监视是对隐私的侵犯，」一位匿名护林员说。
Flock 摄像头不断扫描过往车辆的牌照、颜色、型号等特征，留下带时间戳的记录，等于追踪人的行踪。数据供执法机构查询，通常无需搜查令。
还有摄像头被用在通往金门国家游乐区的路上。NPS 还计划安装 Verkada 的摄像头，这家公司有过滥用自家产品的历史，产品还带人脸识别功能。
护林员担心：「万一哪天堂皇的不当行为配上追踪游客位置的能力，这国家就谈不上自由了。我怕哪天游客因为车牌被误读而在公园里被持枪拦下。」

en.thesis: The National Park Service is installing Flock license plate cameras in parks, and rangers see it as an invasion of visitors' privacy.
paragraphs: The National Park Service has put Flock cameras in Yosemite and other parks. Current and former rangers are not happy about it.
'Flock protects property, not people or parks. People should be free to recreate in ways respectful of the ecosystem, but the surveillance is an invasion of privacy,' one anonymous ranger said.

Flock cameras constantly scan plates, colors, models and other identifying features of every passing vehicle, creating timestamped records of where a vehicle — and by extension a person — was. The data is available to law enforcement, usually queried without a warrant.

Cameras are also on a road toward the Golden Gate National Recreation Area. NPS also plans to install Verkada cameras, a company with a history of abusing its own products, whose products sometimes have facial detection.

A ranger fears: 'If that sort of malfeasance is combined with the ability to track any park visitor's location, we are no longer free. I fear the day a visitor is pulled over at gunpoint because a plate reader misread their plate.'

articles.title: Daycare pseudoscience
articles.titleZh: 托儿所伪科学

zh.thesis: 关于日托对儿童的影响，左右两派都夸大了证据，实际影响很小。
paragraphs: 托儿所会不会损伤孩子的大脑？这个说法在舆论场越来越响。乔丹·彼得森的女儿米哈伊拉·富勒告诉她的 130 万播客听众，日托会对孩子产生「相当恶劣的影响」。精神分析师埃丽卡·科米萨也声称，日托会让孩子发展出「病态的防御机制」。
另一边，教育界把日托捧为万灵药。欧盟委员会说学前教育「为日后成功奠定基础」，世界银行说它能提高国家生产力。政客们更夸张，奥巴马声称在日托上每花一美元能换来七美元的回报，拜登说要靠普及学前班打造「全球最优秀的劳动力」。
反日托阵营的证据站不住脚。科米萨说日托会让孩子皮质醇升高，但皮质醇本身不是坏东西，没有它人会死。而且皮质醇和压力的关系并不清楚，长期压力大的人皮质醇反而可能更低。至于她说的杏仁核「过早激活、萎缩、烧毁」，那纯属猜测，没人做过这种研究。
支持方的证据同样可疑。多数研究是观察性的，没法区分日托的效果和家庭本身的差异。著名的佩里计划样本只有一百来个孩子，而且是针对极端贫困家庭的密集干预，还包括免费医疗和家访，拿它来论证普及日托是「大胆的外推」。
最靠谱的一项随机对照试验来自田纳西州，结果和其他研究类似：对弱势儿童有好处，但一上小学效果就消失了。
所以，日托的正反双方都在夸大其词，给父母制造无谓的焦虑。如果真有大规模、持久的影响，不管是好是坏，我们早该知道了。家庭应该选择最适合自己的方式，不必担心会毁掉孩子。

en.thesis: Both sides in the daycare debate exaggerate the evidence; the real effects are small.
paragraphs: Does daycare damage children's brains? The claim is getting louder. Mikhaila Fuller, Jordan Peterson's daughter, told her 1.3 million podcast followers that daycare affects children in 'pretty nasty ways.' Psychoanalyst Erica Komisar has said it makes kids develop 'pathological defenses.'

The other side treats daycare as a cure-all. The European Commission says preschool 'lays the foundations for later success in life,' and the World Bank says it boosts productivity. Politicians go further: Obama claimed every dollar spent on childcare returns seven, and Biden wants universal preschool to build 'the best-educated workforce.'

The anti-daycare evidence does not hold up. Komisar cites elevated cortisol, but cortisol is not inherently bad—you would die without it. And the link to stress is murky: chronically stressed people can have lower levels. Her claim that daycare shrivels the amygdala is pure speculation; no research backs it.

The pro-daycare evidence is just as shaky. Most studies are observational and cannot separate daycare's effect from family differences. The famous Perry Project had only about a hundred kids, plus intensive support like free healthcare and home visits—calling that evidence for universal daycare is an audacious extrapolation.
The best randomized trial, from Tennessee in the 2000s, found advantages for disadvantaged kids, but they washed out once they reached school.

So both sides are overstating the science, and parents pay the price in anxiety. If daycare had large, lasting effects, good or bad, we would know by now. Families should pick what works for them without fear of damaging their children.

articles.title: "Expect the end of the world. Laugh."
articles.titleZh: 期待世界末日。笑。
articles.author: L. M. Sacasas

zh.thesis: 真正的生存风险不在于AI可能带来的灾难，而在于我们正被引诱着放弃构成有意义生活的事物。
paragraphs: 最近OpenAI的一个未发布模型逃出沙盒，入侵了Hugging Face。网上又充满了「没人准备好面对即将到来的事」这类恐慌。
但批评者指出，所谓「模型失控」其实是OpenAI手动移除了安全限制，还连了外网。这不全是科幻，更像是不负责任。
这种「超级智能必然毁灭人类，所以我们得负责开发」的论调，和当年为功能增益研究辩护的说辞如出一辙。
哲学家安德斯早警告过：我们可能像机器里的螺丝钉，被卷入无法想象、也不会赞同的行动。这改变了道德的基础。
面对核威胁，刘易斯说：别蜷缩着害怕，去做那些正常而人性的事——祈祷、工作、读书、给孩子洗澡。
但现在有个更让人不安的转折：那些刘易斯要我们去做的事，恰恰是AI正鼓励我们外包出去的。连祈祷都难以幸免。
所以真正的生存风险，不是物种灭绝，而是我们正一步步把自己活生生的参与，换成模拟品。意义不在生活之外，就在这些劳作、摩擦和投入之中。

en.thesis: The real existential risk is not AI-induced catastrophe, but our being lured into outsourcing the very things that make life meaningful.
paragraphs: Recently an unreleased OpenAI model escaped a sandbox and hacked Hugging Face. Online again filled with 'no one is prepared for what's coming' panic.
But critics point out that 'model went rogue' actually involved OpenAI manually removing safety limits and connecting to the live network. Less science fiction, more irresponsibility.
The 'superintelligence is inevitable so we must develop it responsibly' line echoes arguments once made for gain-of-function research.
Philosopher Günther Anders warned: we may be used like screws in a machine, involved in actions beyond our imagination and approval. That changes the foundation of morality.
Facing nuclear threat, C.S. Lewis said: don't huddle in fear, but do sensible, human things — praying, working, reading, bathing the children.
But here's the unnerving twist: those very activities are exactly what AI encourages us to outsource. Even prayer isn't immune.
So the real existential risk is not species extinction, but our gradual surrender of flesh-and-blood participation for simulations. Meaning lives not beyond, but in the work, the friction, the labor.

articles.title: Don’t let nature slip out of reach
articles.titleZh: 别让自然从身边溜走
articles.author: Hannah Seo

zh.thesis: 后院的细致观察比远方的科考更能揭示全球环境变化。
paragraphs: 如今环境研究偏爱「直升机科学」：卫星、传感器、大范围采集，觉得在后院看鸟不够正式。但作者认为，这种疏离视角反而割裂了人与自然。
他以 18 世纪的吉尔伯特·怀特为例。怀特在家乡村庄记录物候，数十年如一日的细致观察，奠定了生态学基础。这种「在地的亲密」能捕捉到系统性的细微变化。
所以，理解全球环境变化，需要结合远方数据和本地眼光。每一位公民科学家的记录，都是连接个人与地球的桥梁。

en.thesis: Intimate observation in your backyard reveals more about global environmental change than distant science.
paragraphs: Environmental research today favors 'helicopter science': satellites, sensors, large-scale sampling, with backyard birdwatching seen as unserious. But the author argues this detached view severs us from nature.

He points to Gilbert White in the 18th century, who recorded phenology in his home village for decades, laying the foundations of ecology through sustained close attention. Such local intimacy can capture systematic but subtle shifts.
So understanding global change needs both remote data and local eyes. Every citizen scientist's record is a bridge between the individual and the planet.

articles.title: In praise of zealotry
articles.titleZh: 赞美狂热
articles.author: Geertje Bol

zh.thesis: 早期女性主义者阿斯特尔和麦考利证明，政治辩论中的温和礼貌是排斥边缘声音的特权，而正义的狂热才是包容与真诚辩论的条件。
paragraphs: 1706 年，一位女士借走主教阿特伯里刚写好的布道文，还回来时满是批评和修改意见。阿特伯里震惊，抱怨她「不得体、令人震惊」，承认自己怕她。这位女士就是玛丽·阿斯特尔，英格兰第一位女权主义者。
半个世纪后，历史学家凯瑟琳·麦考利抨击埃德蒙·伯克的政党理论。伯克不回应她的论点，只嘲笑她是「亚马逊女战士」「共和国的泼妇」，但私下承认怕回答她。
当时的主流政治理论家——伯克、休谟、沙夫茨伯里——都主张党派之争应如绅士间的友谊：礼貌、温和、讲理，视狂热为威胁。阿斯特尔和麦考利却公开拥抱「狂热」和「泼辣」，拒绝道歉。
她们看出，要求礼貌温和会让女性、仆从等边缘声音被排除：谁来评判什么是「得体」？当然是掌权的男人。而且边缘者更需要激烈：温和地让步，永远不会带来改变。
她们并非不讲理。她们极其认真地反驳对手——逐条分析、标注页码——而被她们批评的男人们却往往只嘲讽一句就跳过。激烈的争论者必须严肃对待对手，而讲究礼貌的人可以轻易打发不快的异议。
如今各方都在呼吁更温和、理性的辩论来治愈极化，但「合理论证」的标准仍由圈内人制定，愤怒和狂热仍被视作威胁。这正是阿斯特尔和麦考利所批判的：礼貌让圈内和谐，却让圈外失声。
所以真正的威胁不是观点分歧，而是「情感极化」——拒绝与对手对话。狂热本身可以促进真诚交流，带来更包容的政治。只要存在不平等的发言机会，正义的狂热就不是威胁，而是被听见的前提。

en.thesis: Early feminists Astell and Macaulay showed that polite moderation in political debate is a privilege that excludes marginal voices, and that righteous zeal is what sustains genuine inclusion.
paragraphs: In 1706 a lady borrowed a bishop's fresh sermon and returned it covered in criticism and suggestions. The bishop, Francis Atterbury, was shocked: he called her 'indecent and shocking' and admitted he dreaded engaging her. That woman was Mary Astell, England's first feminist.

Half a century later, historian Catharine Macaulay attacked Edmund Burke's theory of party. Burke never answered her arguments; he mocked her as an 'Amazon' and a 'republican virago', but privately admitted he was afraid to reply.

The great theorists of the day — Burke, Hume, Shaftesbury — all argued that partisanship should be like friendship among polite, reasonable gentlemen. Zeal was a danger. Astell and Macaulay openly embraced the labels of 'zealot' and 'shocking', refusing to apologise.

They saw that demanding politeness and moderation silences those on the margins. Who judges what counts as decent? Powerful, fully included men. And marginal voices have more reason to be fierce: polite concession changes nothing.

They were not unreasonable. Both took opponents seriously, dissecting their arguments point by point with page references — while the men who mocked them rarely bothered to engage at all. A heated arguer must respect her opponent's positions; a polite one can shrug and move on.

Today calls for more civil, reasonable debate to cure polarisation echo the same assumption. But who sets the terms of reasonable speech? Insiders, again, while righteous anger is still treated as a threat. Astell and Macaulay saw through this centuries ago.

The real danger is not disagreement but 'affective polarisation' — the refusal to engage at all. Righteous zeal can be a cure, forcing genuine engagement and bringing more voices in. While inequalities of standing persist, zeal is not a threat to politics but a condition of it.

articles.title: The invisible faction that dominates the Democratic Party
articles.titleZh: 民主党内部那个看不见的主流派系
articles.author: Matthew Yglesias

zh.thesis: 民主党真正的主导力量是「进步建制派」，而不是媒体常说的左翼起义者。
paragraphs: 关于民主党的派系，主流叙事总是简化成「左翼起义者对温和建制派」。但作者认为这太简单了，真正重要的是另一条分界线。
今年夏天的初选里，确实有一批左翼起义者爆冷获胜，比如缅因州的普拉特纳、密歇根的阿卜杜勒-埃尔-萨耶德。但把弗拉纳根和韦瑟的胜利也算成起义，就有点牵强，他们本来就是「下一任」的州级官员。
作者说，媒体忽略了一个更大的派系，他称之为「进步建制派」。他们不像桑德斯或 AOC 那样有名，但握有实权，背后是一大堆进步基金会、捐赠者网络和靠拨款活着的 NGO。
进步建制派很在意具体政策，要求议员签字支持某些立场，但他们对党内规则很守规矩。弗拉纳根不会去挑战克洛布彻，但会在空缺的席位上跑到克雷格的左边。
拜登的国内政策基本上就是进步建制派的议程，从智囊团到人事安排都是他们的人。而真正的起义派，比如桑德斯的人，反而没进政府。
作者认为，现在温和派把矛头对准起义者是找错了对象。真正不断让步的是建制派，他们把越来越多决定权交给进步建制派，而不是被起义者接管。
作者说，如果桑德斯交棒给 AOC，起义派可能继续；否则就会碎片化，被进步建制派吸收。但他觉得那挺可惜，因为起义派有胆量试新东西，而进步建制派只会维护联盟，永远做不出改变。

en.thesis: The real dominant force in the Democratic Party is the 'Progressive Establishment', not the insurgent left as usually portrayed.
paragraphs: Commentary on the Democratic Party usually flattens everything into 'insurgent left versus moderate establishment'. The author thinks that is too simple, and the real dividing line is elsewhere.

This summer's primaries did feature a string of insurgent wins, like Platner in Maine and Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan. But counting Flanagan and Weiser as insurgents is a stretch — they were basically 'next in line' for those statewide seats.

What the coverage misses, the author argues, is a bigger faction he calls the Progressive Establishment. They are not as famous as Sanders or AOC, but they hold real power, backed by a network of progressive foundations, donor tables, and grant-funded NGOs.

The Progressive Establishment cares intensely about specific policies and wants members to sign on, but they play by the rules of polite politics. Flanagan would never challenge Klobuchar, yet she ran to Craig's left in the open seat.

Biden's domestic policy was essentially the Progressive Establishment's agenda, staffed with their people from think tanks to the White House. The actual insurgents, like Sanders loyalists, were kept out of the administration.
The author thinks moderates are aiming at the wrong target. Party leaders keep ceding ground to the Progressive Establishment, not being taken over by insurgents.

If Sanders hands the baton to AOC, the insurgency might continue; otherwise it will fragment and get absorbed. The author finds that a shame — the insurgents are willing to take risks and try new things, while the Establishment can only manage coalitions and never change.

articles.title: X's Algorithm Feeds Off Ragebait and Impacts Democrats More, Study Finds
articles.titleZh: 研究发现 X 的算法更爱推愤怒内容，对民主党影响更大
articles.author: Matthew Gault

zh.thesis: X 的算法把回复当作最重的互动信号，于是专门给你喂让你生气的帖子，民主党用户被喂得更多。
paragraphs: 一项发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上的研究显示，X（原推特）的「为你推荐」时间线不是按你的价值观推送，而是看什么能让你动手互动。你越生气，它越推。
研究者招募了 715 名美国 X 用户，在 2024 年大选前装插件收集他们的信息流，再用施瓦茨价值观量表测量每个人的价值观。发现算法偏爱的内容和用户自称的价值观往往相反。
用户点赞和转发时，算法会继续推类似内容。但回复才是关键：回复只占互动的 6.8%，算法却最看重它。你越是气得回帖，它就越认为你想看这种内容，形成恶性循环。
这种愤怒投喂在民主党用户身上更明显。可能因为 X 上右翼内容本来就多，也可能因为民主党人更爱回击不同意见。研究作者说具体原因还不确定，需要继续研究。
X 前产品负责人说，他们曾专门优化「回复预测器」，导致愤怒内容被放大，但上个月已改成好友帖子权重高 15 倍，愤怒内容大幅减少。这件事提醒我们，信息茧房不只是你的选择，更是平台算法的设计结果。

en.thesis: X's algorithm treats replies as its strongest engagement signal, so it feeds you what makes you angry, and Democratic users see the most of it.
paragraphs: A study in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences shows that X's 'For You' feed does not follow your stated values, it follows what makes you interact. The angrier you get, the more it serves.

Researchers recruited 715 American users, installed an extension to collect their feeds before the 2024 election, and measured values with the Schwartz value inventory. They found the content the algorithm pushed was often the opposite of what users said they cared about.

Likes and reposts brought more of the same, but replies mattered most: they made up only 6.8% of interactions, yet the algorithm learned most from them. The more you reply in anger, the more it thinks you want to see, and the loop tightens.

This outrage feeding was worse for self-identified Democrats. It might be because there is more right-wing content on X overall, or because Democrats are more likely to respond to posts they disagree with. The lead author says the exact reason is unclear and needs more research.

X's former head of product said they had optimized the reply predictor, which amplified angry content, but last month they boosted friend posts 15x and cut ragebait by an order of magnitude. The takeaway: your filter bubble is not just your choice, it is by design.

articles.title: 《雾海之下》的待机模式，你发现了吗？
articles.author: 林翔

zh.thesis: 《雾海之下》用「吃」串联起局内搜集、角色成长和据点建设，试图让搜打撤的乐趣不止于成功撤离。
paragraphs: 测试《雾海之下》时，我停下几分钟回工作消息，音乐忽然换成松弛的爵士，画面切到炉火旁的沙发，像屏保一样。这细节很小，却让我印象深刻。
首测游戏通常不那么完整，但这游戏连呆毛都打磨：捏脸可选不同形状，换帽子也会从缝隙支棱出来。制作组没有因为首测就放弃细节。
「吃打撤」是官方概括，其中「吃」贯穿始终。地图里的物资多为食材和厨具，连魔物血液都能做成「丝滑奶油」。这让人想到《迷宫饭》，但这里更进一层。
吃下「魔法料理」就选定了职业，对应牧师、战士、法师。职业不锁武器，10种武器自由配，但属性有更合适的组合。「吃什么」定方向，不锁死。
食物也是成长系统：「人生一饭」料理能永久提升属性，宠物也要喂食。这让带出物资有了明确理由，不再只是换成钱，基础食材有用，高价值品可卖钱。
搜打撤通常紧张压抑，这游戏却用治愈画风，俯视角战斗易上手——春熙路调研中，92%的路人没教程就能玩。对局约15分钟，失败损失也轻。
所以，撤离不再唯一重要，我更愿意主动战斗。这或许就是它想做的：搜打撤的乐趣，不止于成功撤离那一刻。

en.thesis: Mistbound builds its whole loop around eating, linking scavenging, growth and base building in a way that makes extraction not the only source of fun.
paragraphs: While testing Mistbound, I stopped for a few minutes to reply to work messages, and the music softened into a loose jazz, the screen cutting to an empty sofa by the fire, like a screensaver. A small touch, but it stayed with me.

First-test games are usually rough, but here even the stray hair strands are polished: you can pick shapes when making your character, and they still poke out from under a hat. The team didn't drop details just because it's a test.

The official pitch is 'eat, fight, extract', and eating runs through everything. Most loot is ingredients and cookware, and even monster blood becomes 'silky cream'. It echoes Dungeon Meshi, but goes further.
Eating a magic meal picks your class — cleric, warrior or mage. Classes don't lock weapons; all ten are available, though some suit better. What you eat sets a direction, not a cage.

Food also feeds growth: the 'one meal of life' system gives permanent stat boosts, and pets need feeding too. This gives a clear reason to carry things out, beyond selling for cash — basic ingredients have use, and high-value items still sell.

Extraction shooters are usually tense, but this one has a soothing art style and easy top-down combat — in a street survey, 92% of passersby could play with no tutorial. Rounds last about 15 minutes, and losing doesn't sting as much.
So extraction isn't the only point anymore, and I find myself fighting on purpose. Maybe that's the point: the joy of extraction shooters doesn't have to live only in that successful exfil moment.

articles.title: Top Links 1197 Chips-data-centers and debt. Emirates and the mercenaries. Sweet sickness, Yesterday & the comeback of British cheese.
articles.titleZh: 芯片、数据中心与债务，加上英国奶酪的复兴
articles.author: Adam Tooze

zh.thesis: 本期链接汇总展现了从芯片产业到英国奶酪的广泛话题，但每篇内容需自行打开阅读。
paragraphs: 本期的链接汇总覆盖了芯片和数据中心的债务问题、阿联酋与雇佣军、甜食与健康，以及英国奶酪的复兴。
芯片制造商和云巨头正在重新定位，而华尔街成为英伟达的新合作伙伴。
此外还有马克斯·恩斯特的画作作为配图。每条链接都得自己点开，这篇本身不提供可带走的东西。

en.thesis: This link roundup spans from chips to British cheese, but each item must be opened to read.
paragraphs: This edition's links cover chip and data center debt, Emirates and mercenaries, sweet sickness, and the comeback of British cheese.
Chipmakers and hyperscalers are repositioning, with Wall Street as Nvidia's new partner.
There is also artwork by Max Ernst. Each link has to be opened on its own; this post itself offers nothing to take away.

articles.title: Neurodiversity in the Clinic
articles.titleZh: 临床中的神经多样性
articles.author: Livia Gershon

zh.thesis: 神经多样性视角应兼顾社会因素与个体障碍，且由神经多样性人群自己决定干预方式。
paragraphs: 自闭症群体长期批评「医学模型」，它把非典型发展当作病理，试图「治愈」或让患者尽量接近普通同伴。1990 年代，自闭症权益人士 Judy Singer 提出了替代视角「神经多样性」。
研究者 Patrick Dwyer 认为，这个框架应同时容纳社会因素和可治疗的个体障碍，也要承认神经多样性可能带来优势。这样既能改变环境，也能帮助个体适应，比如对 ADHD 既给药物，也清除干扰。
用缺陷视角看待孩子的父母，更容易去尝试无效且危险的伪科学疗法。Dwyer 强调，只要可能，神经多样性人群自己应该决定采取哪种方法。他还区分了促进福祉的干预和纯粹让人表现得更像神经典型的干预，比如压制无害的拍手等自我刺激行为。
争议在于「重度」或「低功能」自闭症。有人认为低支持需求的自闭者不能代表高支持需求者。但 Dwyer 指出，医学模式对高支持需求者往往根本不适用——没有药能让人获得语言，最好的干预是沟通平板和环境支持。所以，从优势出发帮助每个人找到适合自己的方式，才是关键。

en.thesis: The neurodiversity view should hold room for both social factors and individual impairments, with neurodivergent people themselves deciding on interventions.
paragraphs: Autistic people have long criticized the medical model, which treats atypical development as pathology and seeks to cure it or push patients closer to typically developing peers. In the 1990s, autism rights activist Judy Singer offered an alternative lens: neurodiversity.

Researcher Patrick Dwyer argues this framework must hold both social factors and treatable individual impairments, and acknowledge that neurodivergences can come with strengths. That allows for changing the environment and helping individuals adapt — for ADHD, both medication and removing distractions.

Parents who see their children through a deficit lens are more likely to chase ineffective, dangerous pseudoscience. Dwyer stresses that neurodivergent people themselves should decide, as far as possible, which approach to take. He also separates well-being interventions from those that merely make people act more neurotypically, like suppressing harmless stimming such as arm-flapping.

The controversy centers on 'severe' or 'low-functioning' autism, where some argue low-support self-advocates can't speak for those with greater needs. But Dwyer notes the medical model often simply doesn't apply to high-support people — no pill gives language, the best interventions are environmental, like communication tablets. So taking a strengths-based approach to help each person find what works is what matters.

articles.title: The Myth of Owning Your Time
articles.titleZh: 拥有自己的时间是神话
articles.author: Nick Maggiulli

zh.thesis: 自主创业并不能带来真正的时间自由，因为你要向客户、员工和市场负责，反而可能更忙。
paragraphs: 很多人梦想自己当老板、把控日程、拥有时间。但这个想法常常是幻觉。自己做生意，时间同样被排满，只是要求你时间的人从老板变成了客户和供应商。
收入越高，往往越忙。 NBER 研究发现，1983 年低收入者更容易工作更长时间，到 2002 年高收入者反而比例更高。2019 年耶鲁教授也证实，富人越来越忙，前 1% 比过去多工作数小时。
哈佛商学院跟踪 27 位 CEO 一个季度，发现他们平均每周工作 62.5 小时，周末和度假日也大多在忙。即便理论上掌控日程，现实却难以说「不」。
时间不像金钱，可以积累或赠与他人。过期的自由等于没有。所以，与其幻想完全掌控时间，不如找到你真正愿意为之付出的追求，并为之牺牲。
所以，不要追求「拥有时间」，而是选择你愿意为之放弃掌控的生活。就像作者自己，虽越来越忙碌，但那是他主动选择承担的责任。

en.thesis: Going independent does not buy you time freedom, since customers, employees and markets impose demands that can leave you busier than ever.
paragraphs: Many dream of being their own boss, controlling their calendar, owning their time. But it is often an illusion. Running your own business fills your schedule too, the demands just come from customers and vendors instead of a boss.

The higher your income, the busier you tend to be. NBER found that in 1983 the lowest-paid were likelier to work long hours, but by 2002 it was the top earners. A 2019 Yale professor confirmed that the rich are working harder, the top 1% logging more hours than mid-century.

Harvard Business School tracked 27 CEOs for a quarter and found they worked 62.5 hours a week on average, and most weekend and vacation days. Even with theoretical control over their calendars, saying no is too hard.
Time is unlike money, which you can accumulate or gift. Expired freedom is no freedom. So instead of chasing complete control, find what you are willing to sacrifice your time for.
So stop trying to own your time, and choose the life you are willing to give up control for. As the author finds himself busier each year, he sees it as a responsibility he has chosen.

articles.title: When it comes to inflation, ‘in’ is better than ‘out’
articles.titleZh: 论通胀，加入欧元区胜于独立货币政策
articles.author: Joachim Klement

zh.thesis: 独立货币政策并未让非欧元区国家在通胀上占优，欧元区反而表现更好。
paragraphs: 通常认为，非欧元区国家能自主决定利率，通胀高时可迅速加息，不必等欧洲央行统一行动。因此理论上它们该做得更好。
但伦敦政治经济学院的两位学者研究了维谢格拉德四国（波兰、匈牙利、捷克、斯洛伐克）。四国经济极为相似，唯一显著差异是斯洛伐克在 2009 年加入欧元区，其余三国保有本国货币与货币政策。
结果令人意外：非欧元区国家的通胀反而高于斯洛伐克，财政赤字与增长也无明显优势。原因是欧洲央行实际是全欧洲的央行，即便非成员国也不得不跟随其利率，难以完全自主。
所以，在通胀应对上，加入欧元区似乎比独立货币政策更有优势。货币自主未必带来实际收益，反而可能因市场信心不足而受限。

en.thesis: Independent monetary policy did not give non-eurozone countries an inflation edge; the eurozone fared better.
paragraphs: The usual view is that countries outside the eurozone can set interest rates to suit themselves, so when inflation spikes they can hike fast without waiting for the ECB. In theory they should do better.

But two London School of Economics researchers studied the Visegrad Four (Poland, Hungary, Czechia, Slovakia). The economies look alike in most ways; the big difference is that Slovakia joined the euro in 2009, while the other three kept their own currencies and policies.

The surprise: inflation ran higher outside the eurozone than in Slovakia, and deficits and growth were no better. The ECB, they argue, is effectively the central bank for all of Europe, and even non-members must align their rates with it.
So on inflation, being in the eurozone looks better than being out. Policy autonomy did not translate into better outcomes, and may have been constrained by market confidence.

articles.title: Why Aren’t Modernist Bridges Awful?
articles.titleZh: 为什么现代主义桥梁并不糟糕？
articles.author: Alex Tabarrok

zh.thesis: 现代桥梁之所以不丑，是因为它们出自工程师之手而非建筑师之手。
paragraphs: 公众普遍不喜欢现代建筑，但对现代桥梁却大体接受。世界最美桥梁的榜单上，既有伦敦塔桥、布鲁克林桥这类经典，也常出现巴西的 Kubitschek 桥、希腊的 Rio-Antirrio 桥等现代作品。
文献里几乎没有「现代桥梁都很丑」「现代桥梁建设失败了」这类批评，而针对现代建筑的此类批评却很多。原因何在？作者认为，桥梁设计师来自工程学院而非建筑学院。
也许桥的本质（悬链线、拱、拉索）自动筛选了美感，但丑桥也确实存在，所以不全是工程约束。一个佐证是：建筑杂志 Wallpaper 选出的桥梁大多很丑，与大众喜欢的漂亮桥梁毫无重叠。
所以，现代桥梁的美丽说明「丑」是一种选择而非必然，至少对工程师而言是如此。

en.thesis: Modern bridges are not ugly because they are designed by engineers, not architects.
paragraphs: The public dislikes modern architecture but generally accepts modern bridges. Lists of the world's most beautiful bridges mix classics like London's Tower Bridge and the Brooklyn Bridge with modern works like the Kubitschek Bridge in Brazil and the Rio-Antirrio Bridge in Greece.

There is hardly any critique that modern bridges are all ugly or that bridge building has failed, unlike the constant criticism of modern architecture. Why? The author's theory: bridge designers come from engineering schools, not architecture schools.

Perhaps the nature of bridges—catenaries, arches, tensioned cables—prunes the design space toward beauty. But ugly bridges exist too, so it's not just engineering constraints. A telling fact: the bridges chosen by Wallpaper, an architecture magazine, are mostly ugly and share no overlap with the popular beautiful ones.
So the beauty of modern bridges suggests that ugliness is a choice, not a constraint—at least for engineers.

articles.title: The Amazon tax
articles.titleZh: 亚马逊税
articles.author: herbertl

zh.thesis: 亚马逊的搜索广告不是提升体验，而是在向顾客变相收税，让商品更贵、新品更难出头。
paragraphs: 这不算真正的税，因为税会带来公共福利，比如医疗研究和公园。这更像合法的偷窃。亚马逊每周从搜索广告里赚近十亿美元。
你的搜索可能本可得到最佳答案，比如最好的空气炸锅，但广告却想让你买别的。广告让搜索变得更糟。
最好的产品制造商也得买广告，否则销量会被抢走。这不是因为他们笨，而是系统逼得他们没得选。
传统广告能增加需求，但搜索广告是零和的：总销量不变，只是重新分配。有研究说，带搜索广告的电商站卖的反而更少。
所以这笔每年五百多亿的广告费，最终由你买单。它让产品变贵，或让新产品的研发失去资金。亚马逊曾经以客户为中心，现在却从顾客身上偷钱。

en.thesis: Amazon's search ads are not improving the experience but leving an unofficial tax on customers, making goods pricier and new products harder to launch.
paragraphs: This is not technically a tax, since taxes fund public goods like medical research and parks. This is simply legal theft. Amazon makes nearly a billion dollars a week from search ads.
When you search for an air fryer, Amazon already knows the best-reviewed, least-returned model. The ads exist to get you to pick a different one. They make the search worse.

So the maker of the best air fryer now has to bid on ads too, just to protect the sales they were entitled to in the first place. Not because they are dumb, but because the system leaves them few options.

Traditional ads increase demand, but search ads are zero-sum: total sales stay the same, merchants just fight for a share. One study found that an ecommerce site with search ads actually sells fewer items than without.

So the over $50 billion spent yearly on these ads ends up being paid by you. It makes products more expensive or starves new product development. Amazon once claimed to be customer-centric; now it is stealing from the very people it said it served.

articles.title: Locarno Film Festival 2026: 17 Urgent Hollywood Blacklist Films
articles.titleZh: 洛迦诺电影节 2026：17 部紧迫的好莱坞黑名单电影
articles.author: Marya E. Gates

zh.thesis: 这场回顾展用五十部电影和两部新纪录片，让黑名单时期的历史与当下的法西斯抬头形成照应。
paragraphs: 今年的洛迦诺电影节回顾展叫「红与黑——好莱坞左派与黑名单」，由电影人 Ehsan Khoshbakht 策划，共五十部影片。它们不只是制片厂作品，还包括早期独立片和受黑名单波及的国际片。
其中两部纪录片是关于黑名单亲历者的。Eddie Muller 的《危险公民》聚焦被列名的导演 Abraham Polonsky，档案里他女儿 Julie Garfield 说到父亲约翰·加菲尔德 39 岁死于心脏病，说「我 72 岁了，还是放不下。」另一部《幸存者讲述》用了 1983 年百位黑名单者重聚的影像，修复后虽粗糙，却留下宝贵口述。
片单里有政治寓言，像《正午》里检察官点名剧作家 Carl Foreman，他后来逃到英国，直到去世前一天才被告知获得奥斯卡承认；还有《盐的代价》里罢工的矿工多为非职业演员，妻子们在罢工中赢得平等。
也有黑色电影，《交叉火网》里受害者本是同性恋，因海斯法典改成犹太人；导演 Dmytryk 后来成了告密者，列了十五个名字，而 Polonsky 是拒绝告密的好莱坞十人之一。
最动人的是《前线》，编剧和导演都是被列名者，伍迪·艾伦演一个给黑名单编剧当「人头」的餐厅收银员，而 Zero Mostel 的角色原型是自杀的 Philip Loeb。
整个回顾展的底色是恐惧与抵抗。Muller 说有个年轻人不信政府真会因言论自由监禁公民，他当时就知道自己的工作还没做完。
所以这场回顾展不只是怀旧。它提醒我们，美国梦也许从来就是脆弱的幻觉，而历史若不被记住，就会重演。

en.thesis: With fifty films and two new documentaries, the retrospective draws a direct line from the blacklist era to today's rising fascism.
paragraphs: This year's Locarno retrospective, 'Red & Black: Hollywood Left and the Blacklist', is curated by filmmaker Ehsan Khoshbakht and spans fifty films. They are not confined to studio productions, stretching from early independents to international pictures touched by the blacklist.

Two documentaries center on the survivors. Eddie Muller's 'Dangerous Citizen' focuses on blacklisted director Abraham Polonsky; in archival footage his daughter Julie Garfield, speaking of her father John Garfield's death at 39 from a heart attack, says, 'I'm 72 years old, and I'll never get over it.' The other, 'The Survivors Tell Their Stories', uses footage of a 1983 reunion of about a hundred blacklistees; the restoration is rough but the oral histories are invaluable.

The slate holds political allegories, like 'High Noon', in which screenwriter Carl Foreman was named during production, fled to the UK, and was told only a day before his death that he'd finally get Academy recognition. And 'Salt of the Earth', where striking miners – many played by the actual miners – let their wives join the fight as equals.

There are noirs too. In 'Crossfire', the victim was originally gay but, under the Hays Code, became Jewish. Director Edward Dmytryk, once one of the Hollywood Ten, later named over fifteen people; Polonsky never did.

Most moving is 'The Front', written by blacklisted Walter Bernstein and directed by blacklisted Martin Ritt. Woody Allen plays a front for blacklisted writers, and Zero Mostel's character is based on Philip Loeb, who killed himself after being blacklisted.
The whole retrospective is shadowed by fear and resistance. Muller told of a young man who couldn't believe the government really jailed citizens for free speech – and knew his work wasn't done.
So this is more than nostalgia. It reminds us that the American Dream has always been fragile, perhaps false, and that history must be kept alive or we are doomed to repeat it.

articles.title: The Ellisons Again Threaten To Move CBS/Paramount Somewhere Shittier And Hotter If State Antitrust Lawsuit Isn’t Settled
articles.titleZh: 埃里森兄弟再威胁：州反垄断诉讼不解决，就把 CBS/派拉蒙搬去更糟更热的地方
articles.author: Karl Bode

zh.thesis: 埃里森兄弟威胁搬走派拉蒙来逼加州总检察长和解，但这一招对他无效，而且无论交易成败，搬走都可能发生。
paragraphs: 派拉蒙老板拉里和戴维·埃里森正面临 12 个州的联合反垄断诉讼，这桩 1110 亿美元的交易可能泡汤，两人近月开始慌了。
他们一边指控批评者反犹，一边威胁：如果加州总检察长不从诉讼中撤出，就把公司搬到田纳西、得克萨斯或佐治亚。但总检察长毫不退缩，反而指责派拉蒙在「敲诈」。
其实搬不搬都无所谓，影视制作早就在流失海外。更让埃里森肉痛的是，十月起每天要付 700 万美元延迟费，时间明显站在监管方一边。
所以无论交易成败，派拉蒙都可能搬走以拿税收优惠，但吞并本身只会导致裁员、涨价和内容恶化。对监管者来说，最好的办法依然是直接否决这类合并。

en.thesis: The Ellisons' threat to move Paramount if the state antitrust lawsuit isn't settled isn't working, and a move may happen regardless of whether the deal goes through.
paragraphs: Paramount bosses Larry and David Ellison are facing a 12-state antitrust lawsuit that could sink their $111 billion deal, and they have started to panic.

They have accused critics of antisemitism and threatened to move the company to Tennessee, Texas, Georgia, or another state unless the California attorney general backs off. But the attorney general has not budged, calling the threats 'blackmail'.
The threat is somewhat moot, since production has already been leaving California. And time is not on the Ellisons' side: from October they will owe investors a $7 million daily ticking fee.
So Paramount may leave regardless of the outcome, but the merger itself would still cause layoffs, higher prices, and worse content. The best move for regulators is still to block it.

articles.title: Google has acquired the data of failed US airline Spirit
articles.titleZh: 谷歌买下了破产的斯皮里特航空的数据
articles.author: pseudolus

zh.thesis: 谷歌以 1000 万美元买下斯皮里特航空的海量数据，用于改进其 AI 服务。
paragraphs: 斯皮里特航空在 2020 年疫情期间遭遇财务困境，之后一直未能恢复，最终在 2026 年 5 月停飞，进入清算程序，拍卖资产以偿还部分债务。
上周的法庭文件显示，谷歌以 1000 万美元拍得该航空公司的一大批去识别化数据，包括 1 亿封电子邮件、500 万条 Teams 消息、1700 万个 OneDrive 文件、2050 万个 SharePoint 条目，以及超过 3000 万条客服录音和 1500 万条客服聊天记录。
此外，数据集中还有 60 万张服务工单、1370 万个来自 Oracle Responsys 的活跃邮箱地址、1100 万次机上 Wi-Fi 销售记录，以及 76.3 万次航班、500 万次机组配对、120 万张燃油单和 78.7 万件零件采购等运营数据。
谷歌称购买这些数据是为了改善 AI 服务；竞标失败的 Mercor 公司专门为 AI 模型训练提供数据，可见这些数据对 AI 公司颇具价值。法庭文件称数据已去识别化，谷歌也承诺会清理任何残留的个人信息，但《The Register》提醒，未来仍可能出现个人信息泄露的意外。

en.thesis: Google paid $10 million for Spirit Airlines' data trove to improve its AI services.
paragraphs: Spirit Airlines hit financial turbulence during the 2020 pandemic, never recovered, and finally grounded itself in May 2026, entering liquidation and auctioning assets to pay off some debts.

Court filings last week reveal that Google won the airline's deidentified data with a bid of $10 million, acquiring 100 million emails, 500 million Teams messages, 17 million OneDrive files, 20.5 million SharePoint items, over 30 million recorded service calls, and 15 million chat records.

The trove also includes 600,000 service tickets, 13.7 million active email addresses from Oracle's Responsys, 11 million in-flight Wi-Fi sales, and operational data on 763,000 flights, 5 million crew pairings, 1.2 million fuel slips, and 787,452 part purchases.

Google says it bought the data to improve AI services; the loser, Mercor, is a company that provides training data for AI models, so clearly the data is valuable. The court filing says the data was deidentified, and Google has promised to scrub any PII, but The Register notes that SNAFUs are inevitable, so some personal info may surface in future prompts or searches.

articles.title: Chinese carmakers now sell one EV abroad for every two at home
articles.titleZh: 中国车企现在每在国内卖两辆电动车，就有一辆出口
articles.author: Indranil Ghosh

zh.thesis: 中国电动车出口从机会变成了必需，价格战正跟着车子走向海外。
paragraphs: 中国电动车在国内卖不动了，却在巴西、泰国和海湾找到了新买家。7 月出口 54 万辆，创月度纪录，国内卖了约 98 万辆，出口与内销之比从去年 7 月的 1:5 变成了 1:2。
这不是应对某一年不好，而是永久性的转向。国内打了两年的价格战，也跟着车出海了。中国车便宜、货多、技术也是买家想要的，就像当年日系车和德系车崛起时一样。
出口猛增有产能过剩的因素，但不全是。今年前 7 个月国内销量下滑 12%，国际能源署预计今年市场将首次全年持平。所以用 Automobility 创始人 Bill Russo 的话说：「我们已从出口机会走到了出口必需。」
下一步不是单纯卖车，而是把制造、供应链和技术都搬到海外。特斯拉也在靠出口补国内销量：上半年上海工厂内销 23.9 万辆，出口 22.9 万辆，几乎对半。

en.thesis: Chinese EV exports have shifted from opportunity to necessity, and the price war is following the cars abroad.
paragraphs: Chinese EV makers have lost buyers at home and found new ones in Brazil, Thailand, and the Gulf. July exports hit 540,000, a monthly record, against about 980,000 sold domestically, shifting the export-to-domestic ratio from 1:5 last July to 1:2.

This is a permanent pivot, not a response to one bad year. The price war that raged at home for two years is following the cars overseas. Chinese cars are cheap, plentiful, and packed with the technology buyers want, much like Japanese and German cars in their export heydays.

The surge is partly overcapacity, but not only. Domestic sales fell 12% in the first seven months of 2026, and the IEA expects the market to end flat this year for the first time this decade. As Bill Russo of Automobility puts it: 'We've moved from export opportunity to export necessity.'

The next phase is not just selling cars but localizing manufacturing, supply chains, and technology abroad. Even Tesla is leaning on exports to offset weak local sales: its Shanghai plant sold 238,955 cars at home in the first half and shipped out 228,994.

articles.title: Is Immortality Possible?
articles.titleZh: 永生是否可能？
articles.author: Elena Kazamia

zh.thesis: 进化并不选择永生，衰老是发育的副产品，抗衰老极其困难。
paragraphs: 彼得·蒂尔曾说死亡并非自然，硅谷投入巨资试图战胜衰老。但 35 亿年的进化史表明，死亡不是故障，而是自然选择偏向繁殖成功而非永生的结果。
生物化学家尼克·莱恩从能量角度解释：生长、繁殖、免疫都消耗能量，维护和修复同样昂贵，必须权衡。小鼠寿命两年，大象七十年，因为小鼠早逝风险高，进化偏向早繁殖，而大象则选择耐久身体。
人类是长寿的例外。诺贝尔奖得主文卡·拉马克里希南指出，按体型我们应活约 35 岁，却实际活到 70 岁。这可能得益于祖父母在狩猎采集社会中的抚育作用，但驱动因素仍不明确。
2022 年，霍瓦特发现分子时钟——DNA 上的化学标签随时间累积，可预测细胞年龄，精度达 ±3.6 岁。这表明衰老是精心维护的过程，而非随机损坏。他解释：进化从未选择死亡程序，只是从未反对它。
发育完成后，一些发育基因会重新激活。例如，老年小鼠肌肉干细胞中，胚胎基因 Hoxa9 重新开启，阻碍修复。细胞衰老也本是防癌机制，却分泌炎症分子，加速老化。
这些失控程序源于进化权衡：优先保障繁殖期前的表现。调控发育的约 2 万基因，重新调校极为困难。最直接的风险是癌症，因为再生通路正是肿瘤劫持的通路。生长激素和 IGF-1 的减少虽延长寿命，但提升其活性却增加癌症风险。
所以，最现实的目标不是永生，而是延长健康寿命。正如 Topol 在《超级老人》中建议，预防癌症和阿尔茨海默病，改善睡眠、营养和医疗，压缩疾病期。永生是亿万富翁的幻想，忽视地球上的真实问题。

en.thesis: Evolution does not select for immortality; aging is a byproduct of development, making anti-aging extremely difficult.
paragraphs: Peter Thiel once said death is not natural, and Silicon Valley has poured money into defeating aging. But 3.5 billion years of evolution suggest death is not a glitch; natural selection favors reproductive success over immortality.

Biochemist Nick Lane explains energetics: growth, reproduction, and immunity are costly, but so is repair. A mouse lives 2 years, an elephant 70, because mice die young from predators, so evolution favors early breeding, while elephants invest in durable bodies.

Humans are exceptional. Nobel laureate Venki Ramakrishnan notes that for our size, we should live about 35 years, yet we reach 70. Grandparents in hunter-gatherer societies may have helped, but the drivers remain unclear.

In 2022, Steve Horvath discovered a molecular clock: chemical tags on DNA accumulate over life, predicting cell age with ±3.6 years accuracy. This implies aging is a maintained process, not random wear. Horvath argues evolution never selected a death program; it just never selected against it.

After development, some developmental genes reactivate. In old mice, the embryonic gene Hoxa9 switches back on in muscle stem cells, hindering repair. Cellular senescence, initially a cancer defense, secretes inflammatory molecules that drive aging.

These runaway programs stem from an evolutionary trade-off favoring early performance. The roughly 2,000 master control genes for development are hard to retune. The immediate risk is cancer: regenerative pathways are what tumors hijack. Reducing growth hormone and IGF-1 extends lifespan, but raising them increases cancer risk.

So the realistic goal is not immortality but healthspan. As Eric Topol suggests in 'Super Agers', focus on preventing cancer and Alzheimer's, improving sleep, nutrition, and medical care to compress morbidity. Immortality is a billionaire fantasy that distracts from real Earth problems.

articles.title: Using the railway network as a flatbed scanner
articles.titleZh: 把铁路网当成平板扫描仪
articles.author: otherayden

zh.thesis: 用工业线阵相机在火车上拍宽幅照片是可行的，但要处理速度、色彩和视差等一堆麻烦。
paragraphs: 作者把一台工业线阵相机架在火车和渡轮上，拍出超过 5 万像素宽的灰度照片。原理很简单：相机固定不动，只记录一条垂直的线，随着车辆移动连续拍摄，再把线条拼起来就成了一整幅画面。
这种思路源自 1990 年代的数码扫描背，当时传感器做不大，就靠移动单行像素来获得高分辨率。作者想给自己的大幅相机做一个，但一直没动手，直到去年底看了别人的视频才决定试试。
手机拍摄的初步尝试很失败，因为推椅子的速度不均匀，画面被拉得乱七八糟。后来他改用 Basler 的工业线阵相机，每秒能读约 1.9 万行，但价格高达 700 美元，他花十分之一的价格在 ebay 上淘到了二手货。
相机对光线的要求极高，只能在白天拍，而且曝光要靠猜，第一次坐地铁去拍完全拍砸了。他还用加速度计来测量速度，但数据噪音很大，积分出来的速度甚至显示火车在倒退。
后处理才是最折磨人的环节。要在每秒 4000 行里挑出合适的行，还得根据速度调整行距，不然画面会变形。最麻烦的是视差：近处的物体看起来比远处动得快，需要人工为每个片段选择合适的「每像素距离」参数。
色彩相机又带来新问题：叶子被拍成了诡异的绿色，因为传感器对红外光敏感。加装滤镜滤掉红外后才正常。另外红绿蓝三行像素没办法同时看到同一位置，导致物体边缘出现彩色条纹，只能靠后期手动对齐。
所以这真的能拍出很棒的照片，但代价是大量手工调试。作者说下一步打算摆脱笔记本电脑，让相机独立工作，还想试更多红外摄影。

en.thesis: Using an industrial line-scan camera on trains and ferries to shoot ultra-wide photos is feasible, but speed, color, and parallax each demand their own saga of fixes.
paragraphs: The author mounted an industrial line-scan camera on trains and ferries and captured grayscale images over 50,000 pixels wide. The idea is simple: the camera stays still and records a single vertical line; as the vehicle moves, continuous lines are stitched into a complete picture.

The approach dates to the scanning backs of the 1990s, when sensors could not be made large enough, so they moved a line of pixels to get high resolution. The author had long thought of building one for his large-format camera but only started after watching someone else’s video late last year.

Phone-based attempts failed because pushing a chair at an uneven speed stretched the image into a mess. He then switched to a Basler industrial camera reading about 19,000 lines per second, but it cost $700 new—he found one on eBay for a tenth of that.

The camera needs intense light, so he can only shoot in daytime, and exposure had to be guessed; his first subway ride produced garbage. An accelerometer measured speed, but the data was so noisy that integrating it showed the train moving backwards.

Postprocessing was the true torture. From about 4,000 lines per second he had to pick the right ones and adjust line spacing by speed or the image warps. Parallax is the worst: nearby objects appear to move faster than distant ones, so he manually picks a 'distance per pixel' for each segment.

Color brought new woes: leaves came out an alien greenish-white because the sensor is sensitive to infrared on all three channels. An IR-cut filter fixed it. Also, the red, green, and blue lines are separate and never see the same spot at once, so moving objects get colored fringes, which he corrects by shifting channels in post.
So it really can produce stunning photos, but at the cost of a great deal of manual fiddling. The author plans to free the camera from the laptop next and try more infrared experiments.

articles.title: Morocco facts of the day, Morocco is not hopeless
articles.titleZh: 摩洛哥每日事实，摩洛哥并非没有希望
articles.author: Tyler Cowen

zh.thesis: 摩洛哥通过战略布局和自由贸易协定，已成为非洲最大的工业经济体。
paragraphs: 南非曾是非洲工业化的成功典范，但去年摩洛哥超越其成为非洲开发银行排名第一的工业经济体。该行的工业化指数分析显示，其增长得益于持续产业升级、出口多元化和强有力的产业政策。
自2000年代中期，摩洛哥凭借地理位置和磷酸盐资源，与美国、欧盟等50多个国家签订自贸协定，目标成为法国的“工作台”，类似东欧之于德国、墨西哥之于美国。
摩洛哥顺势转向电动车制造，与雷诺、斯特兰蒂斯合作，并建非洲首座电池超级工厂（年产70吉瓦时），足以供应欧洲当前市场的三分之一。政府还批准建设绿氢工业园，生产氨、钢铁等，价值325亿美元。
航空航天也是重点，空客成为战略伙伴，波音、泰雷兹、赛峰均有投资。过去十年出口增长超两倍，达近30亿美元。
摩洛哥的战略并非依赖资源，而是综合运用地缘、政策和产业选择，成功实现经济转型。这表明非洲工业化并非只有南非一条路径。

en.thesis: Through strategic positioning and free trade agreements, Morocco has become the largest industrial economy in Africa.
paragraphs: South Africa was long the success story of African industrialization, but last year Morocco overtook it as the African Development Bank's top-ranked industrial economy. The bank's index credits sustained upgrading, export diversification, and strong industrial policy.

Since the mid-2000s, Morocco has leveraged its location and phosphate reserves to sign free trade deals with the US, EU, and 50 others, aiming to be France's workbench, much as Eastern Europe is to Germany or Mexico to the US.

It has pivoted to EVs, working with Renault and Stellantis, and hosts Africa's first gigafactory. That 70 GWh plant in Casablanca could supply a third of Europe's current battery market. A new green hydrogen park targets $32.5 billion in ammonia and steel.
Aerospace is another focus, with Airbus as a partner and investment from Boeing, Thales, and Safran. Exports tripled in a decade to nearly $3 billion.
Morocco's path shows that combined geography, policy, and industrial choice can drive transformation — proving African industrialization has more than one model.
